title: sqlalchemy store tests: bulk upsert tests need a repeated-key case so dialect-specific ON CONFLICT errors surface
answers: How do I test that setting logged model tags works for every database backend?
I changed a bulk upsert in the tracking store; which test cases must I add?
Where is the logged model tag set test and what does it cover?
body:
Path: tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py:test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert covers set_logged_model_tags with new tags, overwrites of existing keys, an empty list, a 150-tag call that crosses the 100-row batch boundary, and a repeated key within one call.
Rule: When adding or changing a bulk upsert in the store, extend this test (or a sibling) with a duplicate key in one call and assert the last value wins. Review noted the suite runs against Postgres, MySQL and MSSQL in CI, so Postgres-only ON CONFLICT errors appear only there, not on a local SQLite run.
Constraints: Covers the logged-model tags path only. The 100-row boundary assertions track the batch_size used by _bulk_upsert.
applies: Tests for SQLAlchemy tracking store bulk upserts, especially logged model tags.
says: Saving duplicate tag keys on a logged model causes a database conflict error.
Setting tags on a logged model should let the last value win for repeated keys.
Updating model tags fails unexpectedly on Postgres databases when submitting duplicate metadata keys.
search: When adding or changing bulk upserts in the SQLAlchemy tracking store, extend tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py:test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert or a sibling test with duplicate keys in one call and assert the last value wins. This ensures backend-specific ON CONFLICT errors on PostgreSQL surface in CI, which do not appear during local SQLite runs or on MySQL and MSSQL. The test covers set_logged_model_tags with new tags, overwrites of existing keys, empty lists, and crossing the 100-row batch boundary. Guidance covers the logged-model tags path only.
